thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected p99 latency spike for decode-service (us-west-2). p95 ~140ms, p99 jumped to ~880ms in the last 6m. SLO window breached. Auto-pages: eng-oncall.
Alex: @here seeing streaming stalls and lots of tail latency on long-context requests. p50 fine, p95 elevated, p99 catastrophic.
Maria: Confirmed. Dashboards show a sharp increase coincident with a kernel image rollout at 03:12 UTC. New kernel build: kernel-img:v2026-03-10-trt8-compile.
Sam: Any recent config/flag flips? FlashAttention upgrade or compiler flags?
Alex: Runtime logs show repeated "kernel_compile_path: fallback_to_cpu" entries and "kv_cache_miss_unexpected" spikes. Also many TRACE logs showing TRT call latency 5-10x.
Maria: I pulled the deploy diff: deploy/decode-worker got updated to use runtime-kernel:v20260310 with compile flags: "--enable-trt8 --fast-attn" and a new nvcc toolchain.
Jordan: This smells like a compilepath regression for the FLASH/TRT kernels. Could be the nvcc/ptx change or a flag that breaks fused kernels at long seq len.
Alex: Impact: streaming sessions time out after ~20s, clients seeing stalled tokens. CS reported 3 customers with degraded throughput.
Elen: Notified account teams for affected tenants (Acct-42, Acct-88). We're assembling postmortem notes.
Sam: Mitigation options: 1) revert kernel image to previous stable; 2) disable flashattn at runtime with env var; 3) route traffic to fallback quantized model variant; 4) bump up streaming timeouts (temporary). Best quick rollback is 1 or 2.
Alex: We should do minimal blast radius. Plan: 1) set REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN=false on decode-worker pods via k8s env update (no rebuild). 2) If latency still high, rollback deployment to revision prior to 03:12. 3) Notify customers.
Maria: Applying env change now: kubectl set env deployment/decode-worker REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN=false -n inference
deploy-bot: Rolling update kicked off for deployment/decode-worker (image unchanged). 15/20 pods restarting with new env.
Alex: Observing metrics... p99 dropping from 880ms -> 310ms within 90s. p95 trending back to baseline. Streaming stalls decreasing.
Jordan: Good. Keep monitoring for at least 15m. If we see regressions on short requests too, do the rollback.
Sam: If rollback needed: kubectl rollout undo deployment/decode-worker --to-revision=4 -n inference (revision 4 is pre-03:12).
Maria: Patch has been queued: runtime-team will revert the nvcc flags and rebuild in a sandbox. Will also add regression tests for long-seq streaming.
Alex: Customer impact note: Acct-42 experienced a 6-minute degraded window (ingress between 03:14–03:20), Acct-88 had intermittent stalls; error budget burn ~22% for those tenants. CS notified and offered credits.
Elen: Logged customer alerts in pagerduty and emailed the AMs.
deploy-bot: Env update complete. 20/20 pods now ready.
Alex: p99 now ~160ms, p95 ~130ms. Streaming clients resumed. Marking incident as mitigated for now.
Jordan: I'll take primary on the follow-up. Next steps for oncall handoff: create a GH issue with stack traces, hold a runtime sync with nvcc owners, and schedule a canary rollout with full long-seq benchmark before re-enabling TRT8/fast-attn.
Sam: Also add telemetry to capture kernel compile times and per-kernel tail latency (new Prom metric: kernel_compile_duration_seconds and kernel_tail_latency_ms).
Maria: Agree. I'm opening infra ticket to pin toolchain versions and add CI perf checks.
Alex: Quick reminder for handoff: do not enable REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN=true in prod until runtime + nvcc changes verified in staging long-seq test (seq_len 4096+).
Jordan: Taking over. I've added notes to the incident doc and started an action list. Will follow up in the morning with tentative rollback timeline if needed.
Elen: Thanks everyone. I'll update customer comms with mitigation summary and ETA for root-cause.
Alex: leaving final logs and pointers: relevant traces -> https://observability.redwood.internal/trace/abcd1234, kernel images -> gcr.io/redwood/runtime-kernel:v20260310, stable -> v20260307.
Jordan: Passing on-call baton to night shift. If anything spikes again, pager me (slack + phone).
Sam: Thx — good mitigation. Follow-ups: GH-5678 (runtime regression), INFRA-892 (toolchain pin), PERF-123 (long-seq CI).
incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated). Severity: Sev2. Duration: ~12 minutes from detection to mitigation.
Alex: :thumbsup: Closing thread for now.
